newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe says well tests at 3,915 bpd oil.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe says well tests at 3,915 bpd oil.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources and partners Kerr-McGee Corp and Amerada Hess Corp, said its Makmur No. 1 well discovery on the Indonesian island of Sumatra tested at combined flow rates of 3,915 barrels of oil per day and 6.8 million cubic feet of gas per day from three geologic intervals.

One of the tested zones was perforated between 3,658 and 3,724 feet and flowed at a rate of 2,958 barrels of oil per day through a 48/64 inch choke, with a flowing tubing pressure of 485 pounds per square inch.

The Jabung Block, where the discovery is located, is an area of nearly two million acres in central Sumatra, is operated under a Production Sharing Contract granted to Santa Fe Energy and its partners in 1993 by Pertamina, the state oil company of Indonesia.

"This well, our third new field discovery on the Jabung Block, is potentially a significant addition to the company's growing asset base in Indonesia," said James Payne, chairman of Santa Fe. "While additional seismic and delineation drilling will be required to determine the extent of the Makmur reservoir, we believe hydrocarbons exist in commercial quantities. Initial tests on this well are very encouraging." --New York Newsdesk 212 859 1610
